title: Non-Atomic Budget Check in Offline Sale Confirmation
description: The confirmOfflineSale service executes budget adequacy verification and balance updates in sequential queries without atomic database locking or transaction wrapping.
claimed_root_cause: src/lib/services/auctionService.ts reads team.remaining_budget in memory, verifies remainingBudget >= finalPurchasePrice, and updates remaining_budget in a separate subsequent query without an atomic database transaction or PostgreSQL CHECK constraint.

trace.description: Begins sale confirmation with requested price.
Fetches team remaining budget and checks remainingBudget >= finalPurchasePrice.
Updates team budget in separate subsequent query.

evidence.description: const remainingBudget = Number(team.remaining_budget); if (remainingBudget < finalPurchasePrice) throw Error;

blockers: In an offline live auction event, a single human auctioneer typically operates the console. Determining whether multi-operator concurrency or automated bidding bots can invoke the endpoint simultaneously requires operational validation.

validation_plan.local: Simulate concurrent POST /api/admin/sales requests using a parallel test script to observe whether team remaining budget drops below zero.
validation_plan.deployment: Inspect Supabase PostgreSQL schema in production to verify if an integrity constraint CHECK (remaining_budget >= 0) is active.

title: Missing Rate Limiting on Login Endpoint Allows Credential Brute-Forcing
description: The authentication endpoint /api/auth/login does not enforce rate limiting or account lockout, allowing automated brute-force attacks against user and admin passwords.
root_cause: POST handler in src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts validates credentials against database records without tracking failed attempts, applying IP throttling, or enforcing progressive backoff delays.
intended_behavior: Authentication attempts should be throttled using sliding-window rate limiting or backoff after repeated failed attempts to prevent automated credential guessing.

trace.description: Public authentication endpoint receives username and password payload without rate limit checks.
Password verification is performed with Argon2id/scrypt without recording failed attempt telemetry.
Returns 401 error immediately without throttling subsequent requests from the same client.

evidence.description: The POST function lacks any rate limiting middleware or Redis/in-memory rate limiter calls.

conditions.description: Attacker has network access to the /api/auth/login route.

execution.attacker_perspective: An unauthenticated remote attacker submits continuous credential guessing requests to /api/auth/login.
instructions: Send consecutive POST requests with candidate passwords to /api/auth/login in rapid succession.
Observe that the server accepts every attempt without HTTP 429 status or delay.
execution.observed_result: Server repeatedly processes and rejects invalid attempts at full network throughput without rate enforcement.

remediation.strategy: Implement IP and account based sliding-window rate limiting on /api/auth/login returning HTTP 429 after 5 failed attempts within 5 minutes.

code_changes.fixed_code:
// Add rate limiting check before verifying credentials
// Return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Too many login attempts. Please try again later.' }, { status: 429 });

likelihood.reason: The login endpoint is publicly reachable and short temporary passwords have a finite search space.

impact.reason: Successful brute force provides unauthorized access to a team account dashboard or admin console.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by static analysis of route handler lacking any rate limiting logic.

title: Predictable Fallback Secret Allows Remote JWT Session Forgery
description: The session authentication layer uses a static, hardcoded fallback string when the AUTH_SECRET environment variable is unset, allowing unauthorized parties to forge arbitrary administrative or team tokens.
root_cause: src/lib/auth/session.ts sets JWT_SECRET using a hardcoded fallback string 'japanese_places_auction_default_secret_fallback_key_2026' if process.env.AUTH_SECRET is empty.
intended_behavior: The application must strictly mandate a secure AUTH_SECRET in production and throw a startup configuration error if absent.

trace.description: JWT_SECRET is derived from process.env.AUTH_SECRET with an insecure hardcoded fallback string.
Incoming cookies are validated against the derived JWT_SECRET.
Admit requests as Administrator if the forged session claims role ADMIN.

evidence.description: Hardcoded secret string 'japanese_places_auction_default_secret_fallback_key_2026' present in source code.

conditions.description: AUTH_SECRET environment variable is missing from hosting provider configuration.

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker creates a signed JWT token using the known fallback secret and places it in the ja_session_token cookie.
instructions: Generate a JWT signed with the hardcoded fallback secret containing role ADMIN.
Send an HTTP request to /api/admin/places with Cookie: ja_session_token=<forged_token>.
execution.observed_result: The server accepts the forged JWT and grants unrestricted administrative privileges.

remediation.strategy: Disallow fallback secret in production. Throw fatal Error on server startup if process.env.AUTH_SECRET is undefined or shorter than 32 characters.

likelihood.reason: Unset environment variables are common during deployment migrations and fallback string is visible in open repositories.

impact.reason: Complete administrative takeover of the auction management system and team balances.

confidence.reason: Confirmed directly from source code constant definition in session.ts.

title: Static Salt in Scrypt Password Hash Fallback Weakens Credential Protection
description: The password hashing fallback function uses a hardcoded, static salt string for scrypt, allowing precomputed dictionary and rainbow table attacks against stored password hashes.
root_cause: src/lib/auth/session.ts uses 'ja_salt_2026' as a fixed salt string for scryptSync when native Argon2id module is unavailable.
intended_behavior: Password hashing must generate a unique, cryptographically random salt for each password and store the salt alongside the hash in a secure standard format.

trace.description: Password string is received for hashing.
scryptSync executes using fixed static string 'ja_salt_2026' rather than a per-user random salt.
Unsalted hash is stored in database password_hash column.

conditions.description: The native @node-rs/argon2 binary fails to load in serverless edge container environments.

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker with access to exported database records precomputes hashes using the known static salt.
instructions: Extract password hash from teams or admins table.
Compute rainbow table or dictionary lookup using fixed salt ja_salt_2026.
Observe identical hashes generated for identical passwords across different accounts.
execution.observed_result: Identical passwords generate identical hashes across all accounts due to static salt reuse.

remediation.strategy: Generate a 16-byte random salt using crypto.randomBytes(16) for each hash, and serialize as salt:hash for verification.

likelihood.reason: Requires database compromise or leak and fallback path activation.

impact.reason: Bulk offline cracking of team and admin passwords across the entire user base.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by inspection of the scryptSync fallback invocation.

title: Disabled Row Level Security Exposes Confidential Valuations via PostgREST
description: Supabase PostgreSQL tables have Row Level Security explicitly disabled, allowing any client with the public publishable anon key to bypass backend API projections and query confidential actual_worth columns directly.
root_cause: supabase/schema.sql contains 'ALTER TABLE public.places DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY' and 'ALTER TABLE public.admins DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY'. Combined with NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY exposure in the frontend bundle, Supabase PostgREST allows unrestricted client read/write access.
intended_behavior: All tables must have Row Level Security enabled. PostgREST public access to sensitive columns and administrative tables must be rejected by default, with operations restricted to the server-side service role.

trace.description: Public client bundle is initialized with NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY.
Row Level Security is explicitly disabled on public.places.
Confidential column actual_worth is readable by any client querying Supabase PostgREST.

evidence.description: ALTER TABLE public.places DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE public.admins DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

conditions.description: Supabase PostgREST is publicly accessible at the project URL with the anon key.

execution.attacker_perspective: An unauthenticated user or competing team queries the Supabase PostgREST endpoint directly using the browser anon key.
instructions: Extract the Supabase project URL and anon publishable key from the website bundle.
Perform a GET request to /rest/v1/places?select=place_name,actual_worth with the apikey header.
Observe the unredacted actual_worth values for all landmarks before auction bidding starts.
execution.observed_result: Supabase PostgREST returns unredacted confidential actual_worth values for all auction lots, subverting the core auction game mechanics.

remediation.strategy: Enable Row Level Security on all Supabase tables. Revoke direct anon role permissions on places.actual_worth and admins table, requiring all database mutations to go through server API routes with service role credentials.

likelihood.reason: Any user can open browser developer tools to view the Supabase public key and send HTTP requests directly to PostgREST.

impact.reason: Completely subverts auction integrity by leaking confidential hidden valuations to competing teams.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by explicit DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY SQL statements in schema.sql.
